title: Trade as a Tool for the Green Transition: Indo-Pacific’s Emerging Green Economy Partnerships
text:
Trade as a Tool for the Green Transition: Indo-Pacific’s Emerging Green Economy Partnerships

TESS Forum

Martin Keep/AFP/Getty Images

The following is an excerpt from an article published in TESS Forum on October 13, 2026, written by Jane Mellsop, ASPI's Director of Trade, Investment, and Economu Security. Trade and environment goals have not always been easy bedfellows. Measures that support the environment can be seen as restricting trade or raising costs, while expanding economic growth through increased exports has been criticized by some as driving resource exploitation and increasing emissions. By focusing on international cooperation that advances the green economy, however, countries in the Indo-Pacific are looking to bridge these two areas in a way that can advance both policy objectives. The priority of these new partnerships is not on market access commitments that are found in traditional trade agreements. Instead, these new generation agreements are addressing behind the border barriers such as aligning standards, building out supply chains, and using investment as a means to achieve greater collaboration and innovation in the green economy—a model that is better suited to this fast-moving sector. The fledgling Future of Investment and Trade Partnership (FIT-P) is an ideal vehicle for expanding further green economy cooperation given its flexible design, broad membership, and objective of addressing contemporary trade issues. Read the full article here.
